title: Cap. X Arg. X: he who could bend Judas as Peter, yet destined the means to Peter not Judas, elected one and reprobated the other — Ambrose: God calls whom he deigns
pass_a_gloss: Unto these I add, That he who knew and could apply unto Judas as unto Peter those means by which he would be bent unto faith and obedience, and conserved in faith and obedience unto the very end, and from eternity destined and gave these means unto Peter, unto Judas neither destined nor gave them, elected one of them unto salvation, passed by the other, that is, reprobated him. This is that which Ambrose hinted by that celebrated saying, God calls whom he deigns, and makes religious whom he wills. Which words are accurately weighed by Augustine, De grat. Christi contra Pelag. et Caelest. lib. 1. cap. 46.
pass_b_english: Add this: he who knew and could apply to Judas as to Peter the means to bend him to faith and obedience and keep him in them to the end, yet from eternity destined and gave those means to Peter and neither destined nor gave them to Judas, elected one to salvation and passed the other by—that is, reprobated him. That is what Ambrose meant in the famous saying: God calls whom he deigns, and makes religious whom he wills—words Augustine weighs carefully (De gratia Christi contra Pelagium et Caelestium 1.46).
source_text: Hisce addo, Illum qui novit et potuit adhibere tam Judae quam Petro ea media, quibus ad fidem et obedientiam flecteretur, et in fide et obedientia ad extremum usque conservaretur, atque haec media Petro ab aeterno destinavit et donavit, Judae nec destinavit nec donavit, unum eorum elegisse ad salutem, alterum praeteriisse, id est, reprobasse. Hoc illud est quod Ambrosius celebri illo dicto innuabat, Deus quos dignatur vocat, et quem vult religiosum facit. Quae verba accurate expenduntur ab Augustino, De grat. Christi contra Pelag. et Caelest. lib. 1. cap. 46.
